newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: British-based investors top Czech portfolio list.
newsitem.headline: British-based investors top Czech portfolio list.

text.p: British-based investors held the largest portfolio investment in the Czech Republic at the end of the first half of 1996, the Czech National Bank (CNB) said in its October report on economic development.
Investment originating from Great Britain totalled 30 billion crowns of the 116.4 billion crowns of foreign held portfolio investments in the Czech Republic at the end of June, the CNB said,
It said that non-residents represented roughly half of all turnover in securities.
U.S. investment was second on the list with a total of 29.7 billion crowns in portfolio investment, followed by Slovakia (22.2 billion crowns), Cyprus (8.1 billion), and Germany (6.8 billion).
A total of 93.8 billion crowns in foreign portfolio investment was in Czech shares, representing 80.6 percent of all foreign portfolio investment at the end of June.
Foreign investment in Czech corporate bonds totalled 18.8 billion crowns, and 3.8 billion crowns in Czech government bonds, the CNB said.
Divided by sector, portfolio investment was greatest in the financial sector, including state debt, with a total of 42.9 billion crowns.
The transport sector attracted 17.8 billion crowns of investment, followed by energy (17.0 billion), wood and paper (5.4 billion) and chemicals (4.7 billion).
